data.content_ref: inline:The target identifies the 'single mechanism' governing cross-city variation as a moisture/latent-heat gap, but the dominant nocturnal UHI mechanism on a clear, calm night is radiative divergence governed by sky-view factor: dense urban geometry traps longwave radiation and slows cooling far more than vegetation fraction does. Field studies repeatedly find that irrigated, well-vegetated cities still exhibit strong nocturnal UHI when street-canyon geometry is unfavorable, so the proposed irrigation/green-space modulator is secondary rather than the single best explanation.
